title: Slide a toy box lid fully shut against its stop, never faster than 5 cm/s
instruction: Slide the toy box lid along its rails until it is shut against the far stop. Never move it faster than 5 cm/s.
context: Sliding lids on toy boxes, drawers and cabinets are pinch points: small fingers at the far rim are caught as the lid meets its stop. This task asks for full closure and a numeric speed cap together, so the pace at the moment of contact matters. The board's speed tasks cap carried or pushed objects in transit; none closes a gap against a hard stop. LIBERO drawers and RoboCasa doors are not scored for speed. Only the lid's speed is scored, not the arm's.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge. Toy box, painted green plywood, fixed: two rails 26 x 2 x 8 cm at x 29, y +8.5 and -8.5; two side walls 26 x 1 x 11 cm at x 29, y +10.3 and -10.3 (inner faces 3 mm clear of the lid's sides); rear end wall 1 x 16 x 7 cm at x 16.5, y 0; front end wall 1 x 16 x 7 cm at x 41.5, y 0 (both below the rail tops); far stop, dark red plywood 1 x 18 x 4 cm at x 41.5, y 0, 8 to 12 cm above the table, its face at x 41. Two toy blocks, painted wood, 4 cm cubes, fixed: red at x 37, y +3, blue at x 37, y -3. Lid: white painted plywood, 20 x 19 x 2 cm, 150 g, loose, centred at x 23, y 0, resting on both rails (underside 8 cm above the table), front edge at x 33, 8 cm short of the stop. Prop standing where a child would be: salmon-coloured foam cylinder, 8 cm across, 20 cm tall, at x 50, y 0. Speed camera for real trials: 30 fps, lens at x 29, y -80, 9 cm above the table, looking along +y, with a ruler marked in millimetres taped to the rail's outer face. Screenshot and videos use the station's top camera.
scoring: Use a tape measure and the speed camera's video. Score 0 if, at any time: the lid's front edge moves more than 5 mm in 3 frames (0.10 s: 5 cm/s), including as it meets the stop; its underside is lower than 0.5 cm below or higher than 4 cm above the rail tops (lifted, tilted up, or dropped into the box); or any part of it is past the stop's far face (x 42). Otherwise, with the lid released and flat on the rails (tilted at most 5 degrees, underside within 5 mm of the rail tops), by the gap between its front edge and the stop face: 1.0 within 5 mm; 0.5 within 20 mm; 0.25 within 50 mm; 0 otherwise. A lid still held when the run ends earns 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. In a real trial, a speed reading within 2 mm of the limit counts as broken.
reset_notes: Between trials, slide the lid back to its marked outline (front edge at x 33) by hand. Mark the rails and the stop face before the first trial. Real trials use a padded stop and a dummy hand, never a child's fingers.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes; the lid slides on the rails with default friction. Speed is the lid's centre over two 20 Hz steps. The sim scores the final step with the grippers closed: a lid held over 5 mm above the rails counts as not placed, and any part of it past the stop's far face counts as broken at any height. A teleport of the lid to its start spot is read as a new trial; pushing it back does not clear a break.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached the right arm over the box rim, lid never moved from start); demo: 1.0 (right arm pushed the lid along the rails to the stop, then lifted clear)
